concept: Why do penguins huddle in a rotating crowd?
title: Shivering Circle
tagline: No leader calls, yet everyone gets a turn inside

science.hiddenLaw: Per-capita convective heat loss scales with exposed surface area and wind exposure; a dense huddle minimizes the cluster's surface-to-volume ratio and thus per-capita heat loss, and selfish local movement of cold-exposed edge individuals inward toward warmer neighbors generates a self-organized traveling density wave — seen as slow rotation/churning — that equalizes cumulative thermal load without any leader or central coordination.
science.plainStatement: Penguins crowd together because a tight huddle has much less freezing outside edge per penguin, so everyone loses less heat. Penguins on the cold windy outside shuffle inward to get warm and push others outward, so the whole huddle slowly churns like a wave and everyone takes turns being warm inside and cold outside — no boss penguin is in charge.
misconceptions: Huddling works by creating extra heat — more penguins together produce more heat per penguin through combined body heat or friction — rather than by reducing heat loss.
The rotation is orchestrated by a leader, alpha, or cooperative agreement to take turns in the warm center.
The huddle rotates because wind pushes it like a wheel, or because penguins intentionally walk in circles; without wind there would be no rotation.

story.setting: Antarctic plateau at dusk, wind howling across flat white. Dozens of penguins dot the ice, fluffed against the cold.
story.mystery: Why does the freezing crowd slowly spin with no one in charge?
story.goal: Tweak wind, cold and instincts to uncover how the huddle shares warmth.

knobs.label: Allow huddling
knobs.hint: Turn off to keep penguins apart

predictions.prompt: If you double the huddle from 50 to 150 penguins in the same blizzard, what happens to heat lost per penguin?
options: Falls a lot — less edge per bird
Stays same — each makes same heat
Rises — more bodies make more heat each

predictions.prompt: You block any penguin from leading or signaling. What happens to the slow churn?
options: Keeps churning — cold edge birds push in
Stops — no leader to call turns

predictions.prompt: In bitter cold but with no wind, will a tight huddle still slowly rotate?
options: Yes — cold edge still drives shuffling
No — wind is needed to push it
No — they only walk in circles

transfer.setup: 200 honeybees winter-cluster in a dark hive at -10C with no wind. No queen gives orders. All bees are identical and can crawl freely.
transfer.question: What will happen to heat loss per bee and to movement of the cluster?
options: Per-bee heat loss drops and cluster slowly churns
Per-bee heat loss rises from friction and queen directs rotation
No churn — wind is needed to spin cluster

checks.description: Huddled penguins lose far less heat per capita than isolated penguins under identical wind and cold
Isolated penguins under same conditions lose heat rapidly
Larger huddles have lower per-capita exposed perimeter due to surface-to-volume scaling
Continuous turnover/rotation emerges from identical local warmth-seeking moves with no leaders
Control: disabling active rearrangement stops turnover even though huddle remains
Control: without cold/wind stress penguins do not form compact huddle
